subject.title: fix(exec): validate script files outside the workspace root for shell bleed

question: Should outside-workdir script operands be subject to shell-bleed preflight even though current docs and tests say those paths are skipped?
rationale: The patch closes a security-sensitive skip, but it intentionally changes documented exec behavior and may reject commands that currently run.

options.title: Accept Fail-Closed Hardening
options.body: Require the docs update and redacted real-run proof, then land the stricter outside-workdir validation as intentional security hardening.

options.title: Preserve Documented Skip
options.body: Keep outside-workdir script preflight skipped unless maintainers approve a separate strict mode or broader exec policy change.

options.title: Pause For Owner Review
options.body: Leave the PR open until the exec security owner decides whether the bypass severity justifies the compatibility change.

recommendation.title: Accept Fail-Closed Hardening
recommendation.body: Require the docs update and redacted real-run proof, then land the stricter outside-workdir validation as intentional security hardening.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and merged the original exec preflight behavior, so they are the strongest history-backed owner for the security versus compatibility decision.
